records.context: 1. A name that already *is* a microplate sample position address keeps it — :func:`normalise_well` handles ``a1`` / ``A-1`` / ``A01`` / ``aa1``. 2. records.label: spacr.convert.assign_wells#2
records.source: 1. A name that already *is* a well address keeps it — :func:`normalise_well` handles ``a1`` / ``A-1`` / ``A01`` / ``aa1``. 2. The plate format is chosen by :func:`plate_format_for_names`: 384 unless a claimed address or the sheer number of names needs the 1536, in which case rows run to ``AF`` and columns to 48. 3. Every remaining name is sorted with ``_natural_key`` and handed the next free id of that plate, skipping any id claimed in step 1.
records.translation: 1. Un nom qui *est déjà une adresse de puits* la conserve — :func:`normalise_well` gère ``a1`` / ``A-1`` / ``A01`` / ``aa1``. 2. Le format de plaque est choisi par :func:`plate_format_for_names` : 384, sauf si une adresse revendiquée ou le nombre de noms nécessite 1536 ; les lignes vont alors jusqu’à ``AF`` et les colonnes jusqu’à 48. 3. Tous les noms restants sont triés avec ``_natural_key`` et reçoivent le prochain identifiant libre de cette plaque, en sautant les identifiants revendiqués à l’étape 1.

records.context: When normalization is enabled, every extracted image region is divided by the same per-channel scale, ``spec.channel_scale``, so an extracted image region's embedding does not depend on the other extracted image regions in ``crops``. If normalization is enabled and the spec carries no scale, one is estimated from a random sample of ``crops`` -- the stack is treated as the whole laboratory microplate -- and a warning is logged. To embed one laboratory microplate in several calls, pass the same scale to each: the returned ``spec`` carries it.
records.label: spacr.embeddings.embed_array#1
records.source: When normalization is enabled, every crop is divided by the same per-channel scale, ``spec.channel_scale``, so a crop's embedding does not depend on the other crops in ``crops``. If normalization is enabled and the spec carries no scale, one is estimated from a random sample of ``crops`` -- the stack is treated as the whole plate -- and a warning is logged. To embed one plate in several calls, pass the same scale to each: the returned ``spec`` carries it.
records.translation: Lorsque la normalisation est activée, chaque recadrage est divisé par la même échelle par canal, ``spec.channel_scale``, de sorte que son plongement ne dépend pas des autres recadrages dans ``crops``. Si la normalisation est activée et que la spécification ne contient aucune échelle, une échelle est estimée sur un échantillon aléatoire de ``crops`` -- la pile est traitée comme la plaque entière -- et un avertissement est journalisé. Pour calculer les plongements d’une plaque en plusieurs appels, transmettre la même échelle à chacun : la ``spec`` renvoyée la contient.

records.context: **Fonts use TrueType embedding by default** (``pdf.fonttype = 42``) for the length of the save; disabling ``vector_text`` selects Type 3 (``pdf.fonttype = 3``) instead. matplotlib's default is Type 3, which draws every glyph as its own content stream: the file is still vector, but Illustrator and Inkscape open the text as unselectable outlines, and the preference that selects this path is labelled "PDF (vector, editable)". Scoped with ``rc_context`` so a caller that has deliberately chosen otherwise is not changed underneath it.
records.label: spacr.plot.save_figure#4
records.source: **Fonts use TrueType embedding by default** (``pdf.fonttype = 42``) for the length of the save; disabling ``vector_text`` selects Type 3 (``pdf.fonttype = 3``) instead. matplotlib's default is Type 3, which draws every glyph as its own content stream: the file is still vector, but Illustrator and Inkscape open the text as unselectable outlines, and the preference that selects this path is labelled "PDF (vector, editable)". Scoped with ``rc_context`` so a caller that has deliberately chosen otherwise is not changed underneath it.
records.translation: **Les polices utilisent par défaut l’incorporation TrueType** (``pdf.fonttype = 42``) pendant l’enregistrement ; désactiver ``vector_text`` sélectionne à la place Type 3 (``pdf.fonttype = 3``). La valeur par défaut de matplotlib est Type 3, qui dessine chaque glyphe dans son propre flux de contenu : le fichier reste vectoriel, mais Illustrator et Inkscape ouvrent le texte sous forme de contours non sélectionnables, et la préférence qui sélectionne ce chemin porte le libellé "PDF (vector, editable)". L’utilisation de ``rc_context`` limite ce réglage à cette opération pour ne pas modifier celui qu’un appelant a délibérément choisi.

records.context: Object-diameter settings are canonicalized to their stored form first. The subsequent type conversion is conservative. Only ``bool``, ``int`` and ``float`` are converted, only from a string, only when the conversion is exact, and never when ``str`` is itself an accepted type for the structured-data name. Anything that does not convert cleanly is left exactly as it was, for :func:`validate_settings` to report.
records.label: spacr.validate.coerce_expected_types#3
records.source: Object-diameter settings are canonicalized to their stored form first. The subsequent type conversion is conservative. Only ``bool``, ``int`` and ``float`` are converted, only from a string, only when the conversion is exact, and never when ``str`` is itself an accepted type for the key. Anything that does not convert cleanly is left exactly as it was, for :func:`validate_settings` to report.
records.translation: Les paramètres de diamètre des objets sont d’abord convertis vers leur forme stockée canonique. La conversion de type qui suit est prudente. Seuls ``bool``, ``int`` et ``float`` sont convertis, uniquement depuis une chaîne, seulement si la conversion est exacte, et jamais si ``str`` est lui-même un type accepté pour la clé. Tout ce qui ne se convertit pas correctement reste strictement inchangé, afin que :func:`validate_settings` puisse le signaler.
